change: Marked crosswalks between junctions from OpenStreetMap: people cross at them, every driver gives way to them there, vehicles in traffic hide people behind them, and the car does not pass a vehicle stopped at one (BC MVA s. 179(3)). The seeded benchmark runs its 60 people, so where its routes pass a crosswalk the traffic and the drive change.

method.v8: scripts/bench_node.mjs; Node v24.19.0 (V8 13.6.233.17-node.51); one process per suite, against PORT=8331 uv run --locked server.py serving the working tree.
method.webkit: scripts/shot.swift compiled with swiftc -O; a fresh WKWebView per suite calling window.__bench.run with Rules, seed 1, 40 traffic cars, lockstep, save:false; 15 s settle. Per route this record keeps id, pass, arrived, time_s, safety_brakes, collisions and failed_to_yield.
method.platform: macOS 27.0.1 (26A434), Apple M5 arm64; Node v24.19.0 / V8 13.6.233.17-node.51; WebKit (WKWebView) on the same Mac
method.scope: V8 and WebKit; night was not run.

result: V8 70/70 and WebKit 69/70 routes pass, with no red-light or stop-sign violations, failures to yield or deadlock overrides, and no collision in V8. WebKit Toronto s1-1 fails on one collision, shared fault (not the car's): a traffic car from the left lane of a two-lane approach going straight on into a one-lane street merges across the car beside it in the curb lane, as traffic always has at such a lane drop; no pedestrian or crosswalk is involved, and the crosswalks only changed the timing. V8 mount_pleasant, montreal, calgary, ottawa, quebec_city, halifax, winnipeg, edmonton, saskatoon and toronto, and WebKit mount_pleasant, montreal, calgary, ottawa, quebec_city, winnipeg, edmonton and saskatoon, match the 2026-10-27 record route for route.
